subject: Weekly Revision
summary: a mixed revision of the week: fins and lumped transient conduction, forced and free convection, permutations, probability, mensuration and data interpretation, radiation exchange and heat exchangers, and gas and vapour power cycles

questions.text: A fin is found to have an effectiveness of 0.8. This means that
opts: the fin actually reduces the heat transfer from the surface and acts as insulation
the fin removes 80 % more heat than the bare surface
questions.ans: (B) the fin actually reduces the heat transfer from the surface and acts as insulation
solution: Concept: Effectiveness εf = (heat transfer with fin)/(heat transfer from the base area without the fin).
εf < 1 means the fin conducts less heat than the bare area it covers: it acts as insulation (B).
This happens when h is high or k is low (hA<sub>c</sub>/(kP) not small). A fin is normally justified only when ε<sub>f</sub> ≥ 2.
Exam tip: Do not confuse effectiveness with efficiency (actual heat/heat if the whole fin were at base temperature).

questions.text: An aluminium sphere of 10 mm diameter (ρ = 2700 kg/m³, c = 900 J/kg·K, k = 200 W/m·K) at 250 °C is cooled in air at 30 °C with h = 60 W/m²·K. The time taken for the sphere to cool to 100 °C (in s, round off to one decimal place) is ______
solution: Concept: Check Bi; if Bi < 0.1 use lumped capacitance: (T − T∞)/(Ti − T∞) = e−t/τ, τ = ρcLc/h.
Exam tip: For a sphere Lc = R/3 = D/6, not R.

questions.text: A very long copper rod (k = 380 W/m·K) of 3 mm diameter projects from a wall 60 °C above the surrounding air; h = 25 W/m²·K. The heat transfer from the rod (in W, round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: Infinitely long fin: Q = √(hPkAc) θb.
Exam tip: m = √(4h/(kD)) = 9.37 m−1; the long-fin formula holds when mL > about 2.65 (L > 0.28 m here).

questions.text: The Stanton number used in convection is
solution: Concept: St = h/(ρVcp): heat actually transferred to the wall relative to the heat-capacity flux of the stream.
Since Nu = hL/k, Re = ρVL/μ and Pr = μcp/k, Nu/(Re Pr) = h/(ρVcp): (D).
It appears in the Reynolds–Colburn analogy St Pr<sup>2/3</sup> = C<sub>f</sub>/2.
Exam tip: Peclet number = Re × Pr, so St = Nu/Pe.

questions.text: For fully developed laminar flow in a circular tube with a uniform wall temperature, Nu = 3.66. Water (k = 0.6 W/m·K) flows in a tube of 10 mm diameter. The heat transfer coefficient (in W/m²·K, round off to one decimal place) is ______
solution: Concept: In fully developed laminar flow Nu is a constant: 3.66 (uniform wall temperature) or 4.36 (uniform heat flux).
It does not depend on the velocity at all, only on D.
Exam tip: Halving D doubles h in laminar flow: one reason for compact heat exchangers with narrow passages.

questions.text: For turbulent flow over a flat plate (local Nu<sub>x</sub> = 0.0296 Re<sub>x</sub><sup>0.8</sup>Pr<sup>1/3</sup>), the local heat transfer coefficient h<sub>x</sub> varies with distance x from the leading edge as
solution: Concept: hx = Nux k/x.
Nux ∝ x0.8, so hx ∝ x0.8/x = x−0.2 (C).
In laminar flow, Nu<sub>x</sub> ∝ x<sup>0.5</sup> gives h<sub>x</sub> ∝ x<sup>−0.5</sup>: h falls off much faster.
Exam tip: At transition hx jumps up sharply because turbulence thins the viscous sublayer.

questions.text: Two cards are drawn one after the other without replacement from a well-shuffled pack of 52 cards. The probability that both are aces is
solution: Concept: Without replacement, multiply the conditional probabilities.
Exam tip: With replacement it would be (1/13)² = 1/169, option (A).

questions.text: Ten points lie in a plane, of which exactly 4 are collinear and no other three are collinear. The number of triangles that can be formed with these points as vertices is ______
solution: Concept: Every choice of 3 non-collinear points gives a triangle.
All selections: C(10, 3) = 120
Collinear selections from the 4 points: C(4, 3) = 4 (these give no triangle)
Triangles = 120 − 4 = 116
Exam tip: For straight lines through pairs of these points: C(10, 2) − C(4, 2) + 1 = 40.

questions.text: The line graph shows the annual profit (₹ crore) of companies X and Y from 2020 to 2024. By about what percentage did the combined profit of the two companies increase from 2020 to 2024?
solution: Concept: Read the values, add, then percentage change = (new − old)/old × 100.
Exam tip: 36.6 % = 52/142 uses the wrong base; always divide by the earlier value.

questions.text: Inside a closed cubical enclosure, the shape factor from one face to each adjacent face is 0.2. The shape factor from a face to the opposite face is
solution: Concept: Summation rule: the shape factors from a surface to all surfaces of an enclosure add up to 1.
A flat face does not see itself: F<sub>11</sub> = 0. It has 4 adjacent faces and 1 opposite face.
4 × 0.2 + Fopp = 1 → Fopp = 0.2 (A)
Exam tip: So each face sees every other face equally: 1/5 each, as symmetry also suggests.

questions.text: In a counter-flow heat exchanger of 5 m² area (U = 400 W/m²·K), the hot fluid cools from 160 °C to 100 °C and the cold fluid is heated from 40 °C to 90 °C. The heat transfer rate (in kW, round off to one decimal place) is ______
solution: Concept: Q = UA × LMTD with the terminal differences for counter-flow.
ΔT<sub>1</sub> = 160 − 90 = 70 °C (hot in, cold out); ΔT<sub>2</sub> = 100 − 40 = 60 °C
Exam tip: When ΔT1/ΔT2 < 1.5, the arithmetic mean (65 °C) is within 0.3 % of the LMTD.

questions.text: In an evaporator, the refrigerant boils at constant temperature while air flows over the tubes. If the exchanger has NTU = 2, its effectiveness is about
solution: Concept: A boiling or condensing fluid has C → ∞, so Cr = 0.
For C<sub>r</sub> = 0 every arrangement gives ε = 1 − e<sup>−NTU</sup>.
Exam tip: 0.667 = NTU/(1 + NTU) is the counter-flow value for Cr = 1; 0.5 is the parallel-flow limit for Cr = 1.

questions.text: In a Rankine cycle the condenser pressure is lowered, keeping the boiler conditions unchanged. Then
opts: the efficiency increases but the steam leaving the turbine becomes wetter
questions.ans: (A) the efficiency increases but the steam leaving the turbine becomes wetter
solution: Concept: Lower condenser pressure lowers the temperature at which heat is rejected.
The net work rises and the mean temperature of heat rejection falls, so η increases.
But the expansion line extends further into the wet region: the exhaust is wetter (A). Pump work increases slightly.
Exam tip: The lowest condenser pressure is set by the cooling-water temperature (about 5–10 kPa).

questions.text: A gas turbine plant with a regenerator works on air with constant c<sub>p</sub>. The actual temperatures are: compressor inlet 300 K, compressor exit 500 K, turbine inlet 1100 K and turbine exit 700 K. The regenerator effectiveness is 0.75. The thermal efficiency of the plant (in %, round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: The regenerator heats the compressed air from T2 to Tx = T2 + ε(T4 − T2), so the fuel supplies only cp(T3 − Tx).
Exam tip: The regenerator changes only the heat input, never the net work.

questions.text: An ideal Brayton cycle on air (γ = 1.4) works between 300 K and 1350 K. The pressure ratio that gives the maximum net work per kg (round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: Maximum net work when T2 = T4 = √(T1T3), i.e. rp = (T3/T1)γ/(2(γ−1)).
Exam tip: At this pressure ratio, T2 = T4 = 636.4 K, so a regenerator would be of no use.
